title: Plural genitive of -in words: -inten/-imien
summary: Use the -inten form or the -imien vowel-stem alternative in this family: puhelin (“phone”) → puhelinten.
objectives: Use the -inten form or the -imien vowel-stem alternative in this family: puhelin (“phone”) → puhelinten.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: A plural genitive refers to more than one person or thing. Its ending belongs to the plural modifier, not necessarily to the thing owned. Here the task is forming the word.
Use the -inten form or the -imien vowel-stem alternative in this family. Strengthening belongs to the vowel stem of words such as soitin.
keyPoints: Learn the word with its stem; the last letter alone does not identify every pattern.

steps: Use puhelin + ten = puhelinten, or the vowel stem puhelim- + ien = puhelimien.
The form changes the grammatical use, while the word keeps its basic meaning.
Use avain + ten = avainten, or avaim- + ien = avaimien.

commonMistakes: Learn the word with its stem; the last letter alone does not identify every pattern.
Keep the requested number: singular is one, plural is more than one.
A slash between model forms marks accepted alternatives; write just one form.

practiceExercises.prompt: Complete the plural genitive of puhelin (“phone”): puhelinte____. Write only the missing letter.
practiceExercises.explanation: Use puhelin + ten = puhelinten, or the vowel stem puhelim- + ien = puhelimien. These standard forms are all accepted: puhelinten, puhelimien.

practiceExercises.prompt: Complete the plural genitive of avain (“key”): ____n. Write only the letters before the final n.
practiceExercises.explanation: Use avain + ten = avainten, or avaim- + ien = avaimien. These standard forms are all accepted: avainten, avaimien.
